About this report

This report summarizes community monitoring results for this location. Results describe conditions observed on the sampling dates and may not represent conditions at other times. State water-quality criteria are provided only as context. A formal compliance determination requires the correct designated use, required calculation period, representative sampling, and other regulatory considerations.

State water-quality criteria reference

These are general screening references for parameters in this report. These values help interpret monitoring results but should not be used to determine whether the site meets Washington water-quality standards.A formal assessment requires confirming which standards apply to the specific stream reach and using the evaluation methods required by the Washington State Department of Ecology.

Parameter Reference criterion Important limitation Source
Dissolved Oxygen (mg/L) 10 mg/L or 90% saturation for the salmonid spawning/rearing use category The applicable value depends on the designated aquatic life use and is evaluated as a one-day minimum. WAC 173-201A-200(1)(d)
pH 6.5 to 8.5 pH units Allowable human-caused variation also applies and depends on the designated aquatic life use. WAC 173-201A-200(1)(g)
Water Temperature Average (ºC) 17.5 ºC for the salmonid spawning/rearing use category The criterion is a 7-day average of daily maximum temperatures and cannot be evaluated using a simple field average. WAC 173-201A-200(1)(c)
Turbidity (NTU) 5 NTU above background when background is 50 NTU or less; otherwise no more than a 10% increase The applicable increase depends on designated aquatic life use and requires a representative background measurement. WAC 173-201A-200(1)(e)

Parameter results

Air and water temperature

Air and water temperatures measured at this monitoring site.

Dissolved Oxygen (mg/L)

Dissolved oxygen in milligrams per liter. Dissolved oxygen is the oxygen available in the water for aquatic organisms. Applicable criteria depend on the waterbody’s designated aquatic life use. For North Fork Palouse from confluence in Colfax to Idaho border, temperature shall not exceed a 1-day maximum (1-DMax) of 20.0°C due to human activities.

pH

pH is a measure of how acidic or alkaline the water is. Washington’s freshwater aquatic life criteria generally require pH to remain between 6.5 and 8.5, with limits on human-caused variation.

Turbidity (NTU)

Turbidity in nephelometric turbidity units. Washington’s freshwater turbidity criterion is based on the increase above background and depends on the designated aquatic life use.

Nitrate-N (mg/L)

Nitrate is a form of nitrogen that is easily transported by water. It occurs naturally, but excessive nitrate can contribute to increased aquatic plant and algae growth. Nitrate can come from soil organic matter, animal waste, plant decomposition, sewage, and fertilizer associated with runoff.

Total Organisms Found

The total number of aquatic organisms found in the sample. Counts can vary with habitat, season, sampling effort, and water quality.

Total Taxa (Species) Found

The number of distinct aquatic taxa found. A higher number generally indicates greater biological diversity, although site conditions and sampling effort also affect the result.

Macro Water Quality Score

The macroinvertebrate water quality score is based on the types and numbers of aquatic organisms observed. Aquatic macroinvertebrates range in their ability to withstand substandard stream conditions. Some of these organisms are pollution tolerant, meaning they can handle high pollution loads, high sediment loads, and warm waters. Other organisms are pollution intolerant, meaning they require clean, cool, and/or clear waters.
